claims.text: A controlled post-deposition thermal treatment will refine the grain size of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings relative to the untreated as-deposited coating.
Grain refinement increases the total grain-boundary area in the coating.
Increased grain-boundary area enables faster grain-boundary diffusion during high-temperature exposure.
Faster grain-boundary diffusion accelerates formation of a continuous oxide film at the coating–substrate interface.
The oxide film formed at the coating–substrate interface will be stable and adherent.
The interfacial oxide film acts as a protective barrier against wear.
The oxide film reduces adhesive wear by improving load distribution.
The oxide film reduces abrasive wear by resisting interfacial degradation.
Thermally treated, grain-refined coatings will develop a more uniform oxide layer at the coating–substrate interface than untreated coatings.
Thermally treated, grain-refined coatings will exhibit a more adherent oxide layer than untreated coatings.
Thermally treated, grain-refined coatings will have a lower wear rate than untreated coatings.
Reduced wear will be observable as shallower wear tracks and lower mass loss.
Thermally treated coatings will have improved coating–substrate adhesion relative to untreated coatings.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply during sliding wear at 500–700 °C.
Substrate diffusion or other high-temperature effects may independently affect the measured wear behavior.
